entries.title: Contracts is included with CRM: Sessionboard e-sign and Docusign for every CRM customer
entries.summary: **Contracts** — Sessionboard e-sign and the Docusign provider — is now part of the **CRM** product, on for every organization with CRM across the organization and every event. The **Docusign** app is listed in **Apps** for every organization and connects with CRM. Contracts permissions can now also be set on **event roles** (**Event Team > Permissions > Contracts**): a team member can act on a contract when their organization role **or** their event role for that event allows it. The Help Center Contracts section is rebuilt around an overview, one page per way to send, and a permissions page.

enable.path: Included with CRM — nothing to turn on. Portal signing: Program Site settings → Logged-In Experience → Portal widgets → My Contracts.

where.path: CRM → Contracts; Contracts tab on contacts, accounts, groups and pipeline entries; Apps → Docusign

entries.use_case: Send speaker, sponsor and exhibitor agreements from the record, pre-filled, with your own templates or through Docusign, and let each event team manage its own agreements under its event roles.

cs_action.note: Every org with CRM gets Contracts automatically (web-api migration 20261028170000). Review customers who had an open Early Access request for Contracts: those with CRM are now covered; those without CRM need CRM. Event-role defaults: Admin/Admin Lite all four; Session, Sponsor, Exhibitor Managers view+create+edit; other roles nothing until an admin turns them on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any CRM customer who sends speaker, sponsor or exhibitor agreements by email or through a stand-alone e-signature tool.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every CRM customer; especially associations and medical societies with speaker agreements, releases and sponsor contracts.
internal.staff_path: Admin Settings → Products: CRM auto-selects Contracts.
internal.gotchas: Docusign connections are per administrator. Sponsor/exhibitor Docusign sends use the account's primary contact for the event; several primary contacts → the sender must choose. Templates and Contract settings remain organization-level.
internal.talk_track: Your agreements live on the speaker, sponsor or exhibitor record, pre-filled from what you already have in Sessionboard, with the signed PDF filed where your team works — using our e-sign or your own Docusign account.

draft.docs_gap: Training videos for both sending paths are being recorded; the hub and path pages will embed them once published.
draft.why_use_it: Agreements stop being PDFs in inboxes: they are filled from the record, tracked without chasing, filed where the work happens, and can move the pipeline when signed.

entries.title: Gatherings renamed to Field Events across the UI
entries.summary: The module previously called **Gatherings** is now labelled **Field Events** everywhere an organizer reads it: the sidebar nav, the event-type picker, breadcrumbs, tab labels, settings pages, email designer, registration form editor, Early Access catalogue card, Apps catalogue, and all empty/error states. URLs have also moved from `/org/:orgId/gatherings/…` to `/org/:orgId/field-events/…`. The underlying data kind (`gathering`) and feature flags are unchanged.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Field Events

where.path: Field Events (sidebar nav)

entries.use_case: Customers who run satellite events, roadshows, or on-site activations alongside their main conference will now see the module labelled **Field Events**, which more clearly describes what it is for than the previous name.

cs_action.note: Pure display rename; no data migration, no flag changes needed. Old /gatherings/ URLs no longer work — there are no redirects — but the feature was not yet in use by customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer asks about the Gatherings module or sees it in Early Access.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running satellite or field events alongside a main conference.
internal.staff_path: Org sidebar → Field Events
internal.gotchas: Old /org/:orgId/gatherings/… bookmarks or hardcoded links will 404 — no redirects were added. The feature flag id remains 'gatherings', so Early Access toggles and internal tooling are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: The module is the same product you may have seen as Gatherings; it has been renamed Field Events to better reflect how customers use it for roadshows and satellite activations.

draft.docs_gap: The glossary and any guide that references "Gatherings" as a module name should be updated to say "Field Events" throughout.
draft.why_use_it: Field Events let you manage smaller, standalone gatherings — roadshows, satellite events, on-site activations — inside the same Sessionboard organization as your main conference. Each field event gets its own agenda, registration, emails, pages, and settings, so your team works in one place without mixing data across programs.

entries.title: Advocacy for exhibitors and sponsors without the portal: email, export and an open link for Groups campaigns
entries.summary: A Groups campaign now has a **Share** tab. **Email exhibitors their links** sends every contact of every company on the campaign their own link to the company's card; **Export personal links (CSV)** gives one row per person at each company; and the **Open link** lets anyone at a company on the campaign enter their name, email and company to get the company's card. **Copy magic link** works on a company's row, and the card's role stamp (“Exhibiting at …” / “Proud sponsor of …”) drives the default share message. Nobody needs an Exhibitor portal login. Groups campaigns, the email, the export and the open link work on every plan; Exhibitor Pro or Sponsor Pro is needed only to target **By portal** or to show the campaign inside a portal.

enable.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Groups campaign → Share → Open link (the email and export need nothing turned on)

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Groups campaign → Share tab; Recipients tab → Copy magic link

entries.use_case: Exhibitors and sponsors post that they are at your event from a link in their inbox or your exhibitor newsletter, with no portal to log into — the same portal-free toolkit attendees got, now for companies.

cs_action.note: Customers training exhibitors on Advocacy this month (IAAPA Expo 2026, event 6102) should use the Share tab instead of the Exhibitor portal path. Needs the web-api release carrying lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4774 (migration adds Amplify_Recipient_Magic_Tokens.contact_id).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer running a sponsor or exhibitor Advocacy campaign, or complaining that exhibitors never log into the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Trade-show and expo organizers (IAAPA, Informa, Clarion shows) and anyone with sponsor Advocacy campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → open a Groups campaign → Share
internal.gotchas: The people emailed are the company's contacts on the event (Account_Contacts + Event_Module_Records) — a company with no contacts is reported, not emailed. The open link never creates a company: the visitor's company must already be on the campaign. A known CRM email is emailed its own link rather than shown the card. Exported CSV gains a Company column. The Groups tile is no longer greyed out without a Pro module (web-ui-v2 #1194); only the By portal targeting button is.
internal.talk_track: Your exhibitors don't need a login. Send them their link, or drop the open link in the exhibitor newsletter, and every booth team can post that they're exhibiting with your tracked link.

entries.title: Credit Claiming attendance import accepts session codes as shown
entries.summary: The attendance CSV import in **Credit Claiming** now matches a session code exactly as Sessionboard displays it, with the event's prefix (for example `SESS-81`), as well as the bare number. Before, those rows failed with "No session of this event matches that session id or code."

where.path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Attendance → Upload CSV

entries.use_case: Organizers copying session codes from the session list into an attendance file from their scanning vendor no longer have to strip the SESS- prefix first; every row imports on the first try.

cs_action.note: Automatic; re-upload any file whose rows failed on the prefix.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says their attendance CSV import reports "No session of this event matches" for every row.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events in the Credit Claiming beta that import attendance by CSV.
internal.staff_path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Attendance
internal.gotchas: Only the event's own prefix is stripped (case-insensitive, hyphen optional); an exact client session id still matches first. The time-zone half of this PR's title ships with web-ui-v2 #1175 and gets its own entry.
internal.talk_track: Paste the session code straight from Sessionboard into the attendance file — with or without SESS- — and the import matches it.

entries.title: Confirmation-page embed: works with no registrant id and shows a preview of the attendee's card from your merge fields
entries.summary: The **advocacy-attending** embed no longer needs a registrant id to be useful. With only the campaign id it shows the open-link signup form. Seed it with the registrant's first name, last name, company, job title and a photo (`avatar-url`) from your confirmation page's merge fields and it opens with a **preview of their card** — event logo, photo or initials, name, title, "I'm attending" — above the form, updating as they type. The photo is saved as the attendee's headshot when they click **Make my card**, so the real card has their face from the first render.

enable.path: Marketing → Advocacy → Attendees campaign → Share → Embed on your confirmation page → Signup form (open link); add avatar-url and the name/title/company attributes to the snippet

where.path: Your registration platform's confirmation page (the embed snippet from the campaign's Share tab)

entries.cs: Customers whose registration platform has no stable registrant id on the confirmation page (or who cannot pass it) can still show a personalized card: use the signup-form embed with the name, company, title and photo merge fields. Needs the campaign's Open link on. Reference setup: IAAPA Expo 2026 (event 6102).
entries.use_case: An attendee lands on the thank-you page and sees a card that already has their name, title, company and photo on it, with one button to make it theirs and post it, even though the registration platform never handed us an id.

cs_action.note: Nothing to enable. The seeded preview and avatar-url need the embeds PROD publish (lennd/sessionboard-embeds#122) and the web-api release carrying lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4782; until both are live the published script shows the prefilled form without the preview and ignores avatar-url.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says their registration platform's confirmation page has no registrant id, or asks how to show a personalized card without a synced or imported attendee list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizers on Cvent, Swoogo, Swapcard, Bizzabo or an in-house registration site who send attendees to a confirmation page they control.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Advocacy → Attendees campaign → Share → Embed on your confirmation page → Signup form (open link)
internal.gotchas: Needs the campaign's Open link on. avatar-url must be an https image URL; javascript:, data: and relative values are ignored (initials show instead). The preview is drawn in the page from the seeds, not rendered by the template; the real card appears after Make my card. An email already on the attendee list still gets Check your inbox, never a card on the page. The photo is copied off the external host by a background job, so the Creator console may show the external URL for a minute.
internal.talk_track: Drop one snippet on your thank-you page and every registrant sees their own card, with their photo, before they click anything, even if your platform never gives us an id.

entries.title: Docusign contracts sent to sponsor/exhibitor accounts now resolve the signer from the account's primary contact
entries.summary: When sending a Docusign contract whose subject is an account (sponsor, exhibitor, or partner), Sessionboard now automatically resolves the signer from the account's primary contact — no manual recipient entry required. If the account has exactly one primary contact for the event (or org-level as a fallback), that person becomes the envelope recipient and their details fill any **Contact** template variables. If there are multiple primary contacts, the send is blocked with a message naming each candidate and prompting the organizer to choose one in **Review & edit fields**; if there is no primary contact, the error clearly states that no primary contact was found.

where.path: Sponsors or Exhibitors → [account record] → Contracts → Send via Docusign

entries.use_case: Organizers sending Docusign contracts to sponsors or exhibitors no longer need to type a recipient manually — as long as the account has one primary contact, the envelope goes straight to them. When the account has multiple primary contacts, the error message names each candidate so the organizer knows exactly who to choose.

cs_action.note: Behaviour change is automatic for all Docusign contract sends where the subject is an account. Previously these always failed with a 400 unless the admin typed a recipient; now they succeed when there is exactly one primary contact. Live in production since web-api release/2026-10-28 (2026-10-28 18:11 UTC).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer reports that Docusign contracts to sponsors or exhibitors fail with a missing signer error, or when onboarding customers who use the sponsor/exhibitor pipeline with Docusign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Docusign contracts with sponsor, exhibitor, or partner account subjects.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sponsors or Exhibitors → account record → Contracts
internal.gotchas: The fix only resolves a signer when the account has exactly one primary contact. Accounts with two or more primary contacts will receive a 400 naming the candidates; accounts with none will receive a 400 saying no primary contact was found. Admins must designate a single primary contact or manually pick a recipient in Review & Edit.
internal.talk_track: Docusign contracts sent to sponsor or exhibitor accounts now automatically use the account's primary contact as the signer, so your team doesn't have to type a recipient every time. If an account has more than one primary contact, the system tells you exactly who they are so you can choose.

draft.docs_gap: The Docusign guide should document how account-subject contracts resolve the signer from the primary contact, including the event-scoped vs. org-level fallback logic and what happens when there are zero or multiple primary contacts.

entries.title: The Docusign app page shows its real connection state and describes contracts, not a program sync
entries.summary: **Apps → Docusign** no longer shows a **Coming soon** badge or copy about syncing your program. The tile and the app page now describe what Docusign does in Sessionboard — sending speaker, sponsor and exhibitor agreements from the record with Sessionboard variables, tracking the signature, and storing the signed PDF — and show **Connected** / **Connect Docusign** from your organization's real Docusign connections. The **Learn more** link opens the Docusign integration guide.

where.path: Apps → Docusign

entries.use_case: Organizers evaluating Docusign for contracts see the real feature on the Apps page and can connect from there, instead of a Coming soon tile that described a program sync Docusign never did.

cs_action.note: Cosmetic plus the connect state. Live in production since the web-ui-v2 prod publish of 2026-10-28 18:23 UTC (sha 58117bc27d).

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks what the Docusign app in Apps does, or says it shows Coming soon.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization — the page is visible to all; connecting still needs the Contracts feature.

entries.title: Event home: every included tool on the dashboard, the board dashboard for everyone, and Registration in Early Access
entries.summary: The **Today** tab on every event now opens with **Your toolkit**: two rows of tiles, one per tool your event comes with, that scroll sideways. Tools you use show **In use** with a live count; included tools you have not set up show **Ready to start** with one set-up button; tools in Early Access show **Preview** or **Beta** and act through the program (**Join Early Access**, **Turn on preview**, **Request beta**, then **Requested**). **Tools / Timeline** switches to a Before / Event days / After view with the current phase highlighted and one **Next for you** pick. The board-style dashboard (**Needs you**, headline tiles, Submission Pacing, Recent submissions) is now on for every event; the old stat cards, disclosures tile and **Also check** line are gone. **Registration** is a Beta card in Early Access with **Request access**, and the last tile in the toolkit.

where.path: Event → Dashboard → Today → Your toolkit; Preview (Early Access) → Registration

entries.use_case: Organizers who never found Transcriptions, Advocacy, Clips or Galleries three levels down the sidebar see them on the event home with one button to start, and can request Beta features such as Registration from the same place.

cs_action.note: The board dashboard is now on for all customers — accounts that were previously v1-only will see the new board layout. Proactively check in with any customers who relied on the v1 stat cards, disclosures tile, or 'Also check' strip, as those are removed. Registration Beta tile is a good conversation starter for accounts asking about registration.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer says they didn't know they had a tool, or when discussing upsell of Registration, Transcriptions, or Advocacy.
internal.who_should_get_it: All event organizers; especially valuable for customers who have been using only the Program module and are unaware of Marketing tools.
internal.staff_path: Event → Today tab
internal.gotchas: The v1 dashboard band (stat cards, disclosures tile, 'Also check' line, v1 pacing and recent tables inside Submission Forms) is removed for everyone. Only Submissions, Speakers, Agenda, Advocacy, Transcriptions, Clips and Galleries carry live counts until web-ui-v2 #1201 ships; other tiles read 'Ready to start' even when used. The Registration tile stays Beta until the Registration module is promoted (its access hook still requires staff). Transcriptions copy is deliberately audio-only: never say stream video.
internal.talk_track: Your event home now shows every tool you already own in one place — you can see what's active, what's ready to turn on, and request access to anything in Early Access like Registration, all without leaving the event.

draft.docs_gap: Closed: the Event Dashboard guide now documents Your toolkit, the Tools / Timeline toggle, Needs you, the headline tiles and the Early Access actions per tile, with new screenshots.
draft.why_use_it: The event home gives you a single place to see every tool included in your Sessionboard plan, track which ones are active, and turn on or request access to those you haven't tried yet. Live counts on each tile show real activity — submissions, speakers, transcripts, clips — so you can gauge adoption at a glance. The Tools / Timeline toggle lets you switch between a full tool inventory and a phase-aware checklist that highlights what to focus on before, during, and after the event.

entries.title: Get an email when a session is withdrawn, a file is uploaded or a portal task is completed
entries.summary: Three admin alerts that only reached the bell can now come by email: **Session Withdrawn**, **Session File Uploaded** and **Portal Task Completed**. Email is off for these until you tick it in **Notifications → Preferences**, so nobody's inbox changes on its own, and the column switch in the header leaves them alone. **Portal Task Completed** now names who completed which task, and it moved from the **Portal** group to **Admin**.

where.path: Notifications → Preferences

entries.use_case: Event teams that hand speaker uploads to an AV team, follow up on withdrawals, or chase portal tasks can get those alerts by email the moment they happen (or in the daily summary) instead of checking the bell.

cs_action.note: Opt-in per person; nothing changes for anyone until they tick Email.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to be emailed when a speaker withdraws, uploads session files, or completes a portal task (Community ideas with 10, 15 and 8 votes).
internal.who_should_get_it: Event admins who coordinate AV files, withdrawals or portal task follow-up.
internal.staff_path: Event → Notifications → Preferences → Admin group → Email column
internal.gotchas: Email is deliberately opt-in: on by default it would have sent about 161,000 task-completed emails a quarter in the US. The column and category master switches skip these three cells. An older UI on the new API would show the cells ticked while nothing is sent, so the UI shipped first.
internal.talk_track: Tick Email on Session Withdrawn, Session File Uploaded or Portal Task Completed in your notification preferences and you'll get those by email, immediately or in your daily summary.

entries.title: File requests show who uploaded each file and link the session
entries.summary: Each revision on a file request now says who uploaded it, with their email, and marks an upload made by someone on your event team as **admin**. **Last uploaded by** sits at the top of the details. On a request attached to sessions, a **Session** row links straight to the session instead of repeating its title under **Submitted By**.

where.path: Portals → File Requests → [request] → [record]

entries.use_case: When a file comes in for a session, you can see whether the speaker or a colleague uploaded it and jump to the session, rather than guessing the uploader from the presentation title.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks who uploaded a file to a file request, or can't tell a speaker's upload from one an organizer made for them.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event using file requests, especially session-scoped ones.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → File Requests → open a request → open a record → Revision History
internal.gotchas: About 10% of US revisions in the last year were uploaded by an event team member on the participant's behalf; those now read Uploaded by admin. A deleted account shows Unknown.
internal.talk_track: Open a file request record and each revision now says who uploaded it, with their email, and session requests link straight to the session.

entries.title: Choose the columns in the Sessions Summary merge tag
entries.summary: The **Sessions Summary** merge tag now takes options, so you can drop or pick its columns. `{{{sessions_summary:exclude=status,session_id}}}` leaves out status and session ID; `{{{sessions_summary:include=title,starts_at,track}}}` shows exactly those columns in that order. Track, Format, Level, Language, Location, Tags and any Sessions field by name are available. The plain tag still renders the same six-column table as before.

where.path: Contacts → Send Emails → message body

entries.use_case: Organizers who email participants a list of their sessions can leave out internal columns such as status and session ID, or add the track and room, without building a separate template.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer does not want status or session ID in the Sessions Summary table (Community idea, 7 votes), or wants track or location in it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers, moderators or chairpersons from Contacts.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts → select → Send Emails → insert Sessions Summary, then edit the tag
internal.gotchas: The modal that builds the options for you (web-ui-v2 #1186) is super-user only for now; customers type the options into the tag. Unknown columns are ignored, and an include that names nothing known falls back to the default table. The Customize modal that builds the options with a live preview (lennd/sessionboard-web-ui-v2#1186) is super-user-only until promoted; typed options work for every admin.
internal.talk_track: Add exclude= or include= to the Sessions Summary tag to choose which columns your participants see.

entries.title: Send Email: a clear wait message when you hit the sending limit, and a limit that fits real use
entries.summary: When **Send Email** is rate-limited, the **Review** and **Send** steps now say **You have sent a lot of emails in a short time. Please wait about N minutes and try again.** instead of the misleading "We could not build a preview" error; the minutes come from the server (or "a few minutes" when unknown). The limit itself was widened: it is now counted per event, building a preview no longer spends the sending budget, and the allowance is 300 per 15 minutes — several times faster than anyone can click Review → Send — so an admin sending invitations one session at a time, or a team behind one office network, is no longer stopped after ten sends.

where.path: Speakers (or Contacts) → Send Email → Review / Send

entries.use_case: An organizer sending moderator invitations one session at a time no longer hits a wall after ten sends, and when a team really does send a great deal at once the dialog says how long to wait instead of blaming their recipient selection.

cs_action.note: No action needed; the fix is default-on and purely changes error copy.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports a confusing 'could not build a preview' error when sending emails to a large list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer who sends high-volume email batches and may hit the rate limit.
internal.staff_path: Event → Speakers or Contacts → Send Email → Review or Send step
internal.gotchas: The wait time shown is rounded up from the Retry-After header; if the header is absent the message says 'a few minutes'. The new limit is 300 previews and 300 sends per event per 15 minutes, with a 1,000-request-per-15-minute ceiling per IP address across events as a flood guard. SB-10516 (CES 2027, event 6815).
internal.talk_track: Sending one email at a time used to stop after about ten with a confusing 'could not build a preview' error. The limit is now generous and per event, and if you ever do hit it the dialog tells you exactly how many minutes to wait.

entries.title: Download the Ready Room desktop app from inside Sessionboard
entries.summary: A **Download Ready Room** card on the **Live Transcribe** page and at the top of the Live Transcribe Console home offers the installer for your operating system first — macOS, Windows, or Windows on ARM — with the other builds, a checksums link and the version beside it. Links are made when the page opens and work for 15 minutes; the card appears only while a release is published.

where.path: Marketing → Live Transcribe (Download Ready Room card); Live Transcribe Console home

entries.use_case: A/V operators and event admins no longer need to hunt for a separate download page — the correct version of the Ready Room desktop app is always one click away from the Live Transcribe setup screen, with links that expire after 15 minutes for security.

cs_action.note: The download card only appears once the S3 bucket is provisioned and a release is published. Until the infrastructure follow-up (IaaC) is complete, the card will be hidden (available: false). Confirm with engineering before telling customers the download is live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is setting up Live Transcribe and asks how their A/V crew gets the desktop app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Live Transcribe with an on-site A/V crew running Ready Room.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Live Transcribe
internal.gotchas: Download links are presigned and expire after 15 minutes — send the crew to the page, not the link. The card is invisible until the S3 bucket exists and a release has been published (the API returns available: false otherwise). Requires S3_BUCKET_READY_ROOM_RELEASES in Doppler per environment. Ready Room is the desktop twin of the browser Console: same audio capture, same sessions.
internal.talk_track: Your A/V team can now download the Ready Room app straight from the Live Transcribe setup page — no separate link to share, and the download is authenticated so only your team can access it.

entries.title: Dashboard shares: let viewers download widget data as CSV or XLSX
entries.summary: **Allow viewers to download** on a dashboard share link lets anyone opening the shared dashboard download each widget's data as **.CSV** or **.XLSX** — the same rows the widget shows, with the same PII setting, date and time format and 500-row cap, named after the widget. It is off on every existing and new link until you turn it on; a password-protected link asks for the password first, every download is written to the link's access log, and switching it off or revoking the link stops downloads at once. Links with it on show a **Downloads** badge in the Share dialog.

enable.path: Dashboard → Settings → Share → Create New Link → Allow viewers to download

where.path: Shared dashboard page → Download menu on each widget

entries.use_case: Organizers who share live dashboards with clients or stakeholders can now let those viewers download widget data directly, without needing admin access or a separate report share. The toggle is off by default, so existing shares stay view-only until an organizer deliberately enables it.

cs_action.note: Staff turn Allow viewers to download on per share link in the dashboard's Share dialog (super-user control). ICS Events (US) was the originating request and has 2 dashboard shares — reach out once it is on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer says their clients want to download data from a shared dashboard, or when they are using dashboard shares instead of report shares.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who share dashboards externally with clients, sponsors, or leadership who need offline copies of the data.
internal.staff_path: Dashboard → Settings → Share → link row → Allow viewers to download (super user)
internal.gotchas: The checkbox and the per-link switch are super-user-only in the Share dialog for now (web-ui-v2 #1192); customers see the viewer side (Download menus) once staff turn it on for a link. All 13 existing dashboard shares (12 US, 1 EU) default to off. Downloads are capped at 500 rows (the widget's display limit). There is no 'Download all widgets'; each widget is downloaded individually.
internal.talk_track: If your clients are viewing a shared dashboard and want to take the data away in a spreadsheet, you can now flip a switch on that share link to let them download any widget as CSV or XLSX — same data they see on screen, same formatting, and you can turn it off at any time.

entries.title: Portal: Edit Submission when the form is open, no empty Submission Tasks, and a Show Tasks Widget setting
entries.summary: The button on a portal session now reads **Edit Submission** while the submission form still accepts changes, and **View Submission** once the form has closed or the submission was withdrawn. Portal users who have contact tasks but no submission tasks no longer see an empty **Submission Tasks** section. A new **Show Tasks Widget** setting on the portal's **Configuration** step hides the Tasks card on the portal home and **Tasks** in the portal navigation, the same way the Sessions widget can be hidden.

where.path: Portal → Configuration → Show Tasks Widget; portal home → Tasks card; session → Edit Submission / View Submission

entries.use_case: Speakers who can still edit their submission now see a clearly labelled **Edit Submission** button instead of the ambiguous "View Submission" label, reducing confusion and support requests. Organizers who do not use submission tasks can hide the Tasks widget entirely so the portal home stays clean and relevant for their speakers.

cs_action.note: All three changes are on by default. Show Tasks Widget is on for every existing portal, so nothing disappears until an organizer turns it off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why speakers are confused about whether they can edit their submission, or when a customer wants to simplify the portal home for events that don't use submission tasks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the speaker/contact portal with submission forms or portal tasks.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portal → Configuration → Show Tasks Widget
internal.gotchas: The Edit Submission label follows the same rules as the submission form itself: form open, not past its last close date, submission not withdrawn, and the form not deleted. A form the organizer deleted still shows View Submission.
internal.talk_track: Speakers told us the 'View Submission' button was confusing — they didn't know they could still edit. Now the button says 'Edit Submission' when the form is open, and 'View Submission' when it's closed. We also cleaned up the Tasks panel so speakers who have no submission tasks don't see an empty section, and gave organizers a toggle to hide the Tasks widget entirely if they don't use it.

entries.title: Put portal pages and files in the order speakers should read them
entries.summary: **Portals → Resources** and **Portals → Files** now have an order of their own. Drag a page or file by its handle, or use **Move up** and **Move down**, and the new order saves at once and applies to every portal of the event, so the onboarding checklist sits first and the venue map last without editing each portal's **Customize → Resources**. Reordering pauses while a search filters the list.

where.path: Program → Portals → Resources / Files (drag handle, Move up, Move down)

entries.use_case: What matters most at the start of speaker onboarding is obsolete a month later. Instead of rebuilding each portal's resource list, the team drags the current priority to the top once and every portal follows.

cs_action.note: On for everyone. The release also backfilled every event's library order from the order its portals already used, so nothing moved on the day.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why the Resources page lists pages in a strange order (it used to be by title, Z→A) or wants the most important resource shown first.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event with more than a handful of portal pages or files; Eudēmonia raised it.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → Resources or Files → drag handle
internal.gotchas: Needs permission to update portal tasks. The same release lets staff assign pages and files to individual contacts, sessions or groups (checkbox per row, Assign to contacts, sessions or groups, an Everyone / N assigned badge) — super-user-only for now; promote the gate before telling customers. Per-portal Customize → Resources order still works and is re-sequenced to follow the library order.
internal.talk_track: You can now drag your portal resources into the order you want speakers to read them, once, and every portal follows.

entries.title: Weekly portal summary skips people with nothing left to do
entries.summary: The Monday **Weekly Digest Email** now goes only to portal users who still have something outstanding — an incomplete task or form, or a file request with nothing uploaded or a denied upload. When any of a person's items are marked **Required**, only those count. A comment on their session in the last 7 days still sends it, and a denied file reads **Denied - Please Resubmit**. **Send → Send Portal Summary** in Contacts always sends.

where.path: Participants' Monday Weekly Digest Email (portal → Configuration → Portal Notifications → Weekly Digest Email)

entries.use_case: Speakers who have finished everything stop getting a Monday reminder they do not need, so the people who still owe you something are more likely to read theirs.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Expect fewer weekly digest sends on events where most participants are done; that drop is the point of the change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or speaker complains about weekly reminders after finishing every task, or asks why weekly digest volume dropped.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with Weekly Digest Email on for a portal.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → ⋯ → Preview weekly reminders (staff only) lists exactly who the next Monday run will email.
internal.gotchas: Required-only counting is per person: if none of that person's items are marked Required, every item counts, so optional items still trigger the email. A file waiting for review or approved does not count; a denied file does. A session comment in the last 7 days always sends. The manual Send Portal Summary from Contacts is unchanged and always sends.
internal.talk_track: The weekly digest now only goes to people who still have something to do. If you want to nudge someone anyway, Send Portal Summary from Contacts still sends to anyone you pick.

entries.title: Sort a table from its column header
entries.summary: Open a column header's menu and choose **Sort Ascending**, **Sort Descending** or **Clear Sort** on **Contacts**, **Sessions > Submissions**, **Agenda > List**, **Applications** and the follow-up form, file request and organization portal form submissions tables. The sort shows in the **Sort** panel and marks the view as changed: **Save Changes** keeps it, **Reset Changes** puts the saved sort back.

where.path: Any listed table → column header menu

entries.use_case: Reordering a long contacts or submissions list is one click on the column instead of a trip into the Sort panel.

cs_action.note: On for every admin. Column pinning in the same menu is staff-only for now — do not demo or promise it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a faster way to sort a table, or says sorting from the header 'should just work'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organizer working in grids.
internal.staff_path: Same as the customer; staff also see Pin column (super users only).
internal.gotchas: A header sort replaces the current sort list with that one column; stacking up to three sorts is still done in the Sort panel. Clear Sort removes only that column. Columns that cannot be sorted show no sort actions. Reset Changes on Sessions and Agenda now restores the saved view's full state.
internal.talk_track: You can now sort any table by clicking its column header — and save the sort with your view.

entries.title: Expo due dates now save correctly
entries.summary: Saving a **Due date** on an Exhibitor Manual section or an Expo Deadline no longer returns an error. The date pickers previously sent a timestamp the API rejected; they now send a valid date-time value and display the same local day back to the organizer.

where.path: Expo → Deadlines; Expo → Exhibitor Manual; Expo → Shop

entries.use_case: Organizers setting deadlines for exhibitor manual sections or adding Expo deadlines can now pick a due date and save without hitting an error, so exhibitor timelines can be communicated through the portal as intended.

cs_action.note: Bug fix; no configuration needed. Affects any event using the Expo beta with due dates on manual sections or deadlines.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that saving a due date in Expo Deadlines or the Exhibitor Manual throws an error.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Expo beta who sets due dates on exhibitor manual sections or deadlines.
internal.staff_path: Event → Expo → Deadlines or Exhibitor Manual
internal.gotchas: The fix also corrects the Shop 'Order by' date display, which was affected by the same formatting issue even though the API did not reject it.
internal.talk_track: A date-format mismatch was causing a 400 error when saving due dates in Expo; this is now resolved and no action is needed on the customer's side.

draft.docs_gap: The Deadlines and Exhibitor Manual guides should note that due dates are stored and displayed in the organizer's local timezone.

entries.title: Event team members can now access Contracts without an org role
entries.summary: Contracts permissions now honour **org role OR event role**, so event team members who hold a Contracts permission on a specific event can view, send, and manage contracts for that event without needing an organisation-level role. The **Permissions** editor for event roles now includes a **Contracts** module (when the org has the Contracts feature), and default event roles — Admin, Admin Lite, Session Manager, Sponsor Manager, and Exhibitor Manager — are seeded with appropriate Contracts permissions out of the box.

where.path: Event → Settings → Permissions → Event Roles → Contracts

entries.use_case: Organisations that delegate event management to coordinators who don't hold an org-level role can now grant those team members Contracts access scoped to their specific event, so they can send and track speaker contracts without broader org permissions.

cs_action.note: Default event roles (Admin, Admin Lite, Session/Sponsor/Exhibitor Manager) are seeded with Contracts permissions automatically via migration. Verify seeded permissions look correct for each customer's role setup before announcing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says their event coordinators can't see or send contracts, or when onboarding a team that uses event-scoped roles heavily.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Contracts (beta) who has event team members without org roles — common for large orgs with per-event coordinators.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Permissions → Event Roles → Contracts
internal.gotchas: Creating a contract requires an event to be associated with it when the user only has event-level access — attempting to create a contract with no event on event-only access returns a 400 error. Template and Contract settings writes remain org-level only; event-role users can read templates (so the Send dialog works) but cannot create or edit them.
internal.talk_track: Previously, anyone who needed to send or manage contracts had to have an org-level Contracts role. Now you can grant Contracts access at the event level, so your per-event coordinators can handle contracts for their event without touching anything else in the org.

draft.docs_gap: The Contracts permissions section of the guide should be updated to explain the org-role-OR-event-role model, list the new event-level permission slugs, describe the default seeded permissions per event role, and note that contract creation requires an event association when using event-only access.
draft.why_use_it: Contracts lets you send, track, and collect signatures on speaker and participant agreements directly inside Sessionboard — using either Sessionboard's built-in e-sign or Docusign. Event-scoped permissions mean you can give each event's team exactly the Contracts access they need, keeping sensitive org-wide data separate while letting coordinators do their jobs.

entries.title: Four credit-claiming fixes: partial claims, time zones, badge visibility, and claim-site settings
entries.summary: Four bugs in the credit-claiming flow are resolved. (1) Attendees who already claimed one credential on a session can now claim a second — a **Claim \<credential\>** button appears next to the **Claimed** badge for any credential not yet claimed, and only the new credential is submitted. (2) Session times, day tabs, "Claiming opens …" text, and claim-window editors now display times in the event's time zone with a zone label (e.g. "2:00 PM – 3:00 PM PST") instead of the browser's local time; the web transcript and certificates already used the event zone, so all surfaces now agree. (3) The **Credit claimed** badge on the field-event guest list (**People** tab) is no longer hidden inside the truncated name line — it appears on its own line below the email address. (4) The **Claim site** settings panel saves correctly regardless of whether the server returns a `catalog` field, preventing a 400 error that blocked saving claim-site settings in some configurations.

where.path: Learning → Claim site; Program → Settings → Credits → Claiming; Field Events → People

entries.use_case: Attendees at CME or CE events who hold multiple credentials (e.g. ACPE and ABIM) can now claim each one independently on the same session without removing a prior claim. Organizers also see accurate event-zone times in every claiming surface, so the claim page, transcript, and certificates all agree.

cs_action.note: All four fixes are default-on for orgs with the credit-claiming beta. No action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that attendees couldn't claim a second credential, that claim times didn't match their certificates, that the credit badge was invisible on the field-event guest list, or that saving claim-site settings returned an error.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using the Credit Claiming beta, especially those with multi-credential CME/CE programs or field events.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Claim site; Program → Settings → Credits → Claiming; Field Events → People
internal.gotchas: Time-zone labels on the claim page and claim-window editors require the web-api to return event_timezone in the claim and claim-site responses (web-api #4756). Until that API release is live, times fall back silently to the browser zone with no label — the current behaviour — so there is no regression. The catalog-compat fix is also a no-op once the matching API release ships.
internal.talk_track: We fixed four rough edges in credit claiming: attendees can now pick up a second credential on a session they already partially claimed; all times on the claim page and editors now match the event's time zone (and the PDF); the credit badge is visible on the field-event guest list; and the claim-site settings panel saves reliably.

draft.docs_gap: The credit-claiming guide should document that (a) attendees can claim multiple credentials on the same session independently, (b) all claim-site times display in the event's configured time zone with a zone label, and (c) the claim-window editors show a "Times are in …" note.

entries.title: Event Today dashboard shows accurate submission pacing, registered KPI, toolkit counts, and In the Room value
entries.summary: The board-style **Today** dashboard now shows consistent numbers across all its cards. The **Submission Pacing** footnote uses the same definition as the **Submissions** card (sessions submitted through a live form), so both figures always agree. The **Registered** KPI tile compares the current count against the previous edition when that data is available. **Your toolkit** tiles for email campaigns, contracts, disclosures, surveys, embeds, and registrations now display a count alongside the tile status; a tile that cannot read its count stays on **Ready to start**. The **In the Room** value loads correctly once room-fit data is available.

where.path: Event sidebar → Dashboard → Today

entries.use_case: Organizers who rely on the Today dashboard to track event health at a glance will now see submission pacing, registered attendees, toolkit progress, and room-fit values that are consistent and accurate, reducing the need to cross-check numbers in other modules.

cs_action.note: All fixes are default-on corrections to existing dashboard cards. The Registered vs. last-edition comparison requires the lens API endpoint to be live; until then the tile shows the attendee total without a comparison, as before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that the Submissions card and the Pacing footnote show different numbers, or that toolkit tiles show no counts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the board-style Today dashboard, especially those tracking submission pacing or toolkit readiness.
internal.staff_path: Event sidebar → Dashboard → Today
internal.gotchas: The Registered vs. last-edition comparison (lens KPI) only appears after the companion API endpoint ships. The In the Room value requires Signals to be enabled on the event.
internal.talk_track: The Today dashboard now keeps all its numbers in sync — pacing and submissions use the same definition, toolkit tiles show real counts, and the room-fit value loads reliably.

draft.docs_gap: The Event Dashboard guide should document the Submission Pacing footnote definition, the Registered vs. last-edition KPI comparison, the toolkit tile counts, and the In the Room value source so organizers understand what each number represents.
draft.why_use_it: The Today dashboard gives organizers a single view of the most important event health signals — submission momentum, attendee registration, speaker task progress, and room fit — without navigating across modules. Use it at the start of each day to spot what needs attention and confirm that key milestones are on track.

entries.title: Organize email templates into folders
entries.summary: A folder rail on **Email Templates** (event and org) lets you create, rename, reorder, and delete folders. Each template row gains a **Folder** column and a cross-folder search box. Select one or more templates and choose **Move to folder** from the bulk action bar or the row **⋯** menu. **Add Template** while a folder is selected files the new template there automatically. In the Send Email modal, Campaign wizard **Start from a template**, and Automations email action, templates are grouped under their folder names once any template has been filed.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Email Template Folders; then Event Settings → Email Templates or Org Settings → Email Templates

where.path: Event Settings → Email Templates  /  Org Settings → Email Templates

entries.use_case: Events with dozens or hundreds of custom email templates can group them into named folders — such as "Reminders", "Confirmations", or "Lifecycle" — so team members find the right template quickly when sending emails, building campaigns, or configuring automations.

cs_action.note: Feature is behind a super-user flag (useSuperUser / useTemplateFoldersEnabled). Requires web-api PR #4765 to be deployed first. Promoting to GA is a one-line flag change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer mentions difficulty finding templates or reports having 20+ custom templates on an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events or orgs with large template libraries — p99 is 38 templates per event; one event has 502.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Email Templates (folder rail appears only for super users while in staff rollout)
internal.gotchas: Lifecycle (system) emails cannot be filed into folders and have no checkbox; they drop out of a folder view but are still found by search. The SaveAsTemplate dialog (campaign → template) always lands in Unfiled. Template PUT never sends folderId, so editing a template does not change its folder. Pickers stay flat until at least one template is filed.
internal.talk_track: If you have a lot of custom email templates and your team struggles to find the right one when sending, folders let you group them by purpose — Reminders, Confirmations, Speaker comms — and those groups show up everywhere you pick a template.

draft.docs_gap: The Email Templates guide needs a new "Folders" section covering how to create, rename, reorder, and delete folders; how to move templates individually and in bulk; how the cross-folder search works; and how grouped templates appear in the Send Email modal, Campaign wizard, and Automations email action.
draft.why_use_it: Email template folders let you organize a large library of custom templates into named groups so your team spends less time scrolling and more time sending. Folders appear in every template picker — Send Email, Campaign wizard, and Automations — so the right template is always easy to find regardless of where you are working. A cross-folder search matches on title, subject, and folder name, so nothing gets buried even in the largest libraries.

entries.title: Assignment rule editor now shows saved values for fields from other events
entries.summary: When editing a **Field Rule** assignment rule in an event that is different from the one where the rule's custom fields were created, the condition and target pickers now display the previously saved values and their option lists correctly. Previously, every picker reset to **Select a value** with an empty dropdown. A stale option (one removed from the field after the rule was saved) now appears as **\<label\> (not an option anymore)** so it is visible and can be replaced rather than silently dropped.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Field Rules; then Settings → Library → Fields → Field rules

where.path: Settings → Library → Fields → Field rules

entries.use_case: Organizations that share custom dropdown or checkbox fields across multiple events and manage assignment rules from a central event will now see their saved rule conditions and targets correctly when they open the rule editor from any event — not just the event where the fields were originally created.

cs_action.note: Rules were always applying correctly at runtime — only the editor display was broken. No data loss occurred. Fix requires both the API PR (sessionboard-web-api#4789) and this UI PR to be deployed; the API change ships first in the next release cut.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with Field Rules enabled reports that their assignment rule editor shows blank dropdowns or 'Select a value' for saved conditions after switching events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Field Rules (on_request) who have custom fields scoped to one event but manage rules from another event — common in multi-event orgs with shared consent or compliance fields.
internal.staff_path: Settings → Library → Fields → Field rules → edit any assignment rule
internal.gotchas: The fix is a no-op until the companion API PR (sessionboard-web-api#4789) is deployed. Until then, the editor behaves exactly as before — no regression, but no fix either. Both PRs must be live for the customer-visible fix to take effect.
internal.talk_track: The rule editor was showing blank pickers when fields belonged to a different event than the one currently open. The rules themselves were always running correctly and writing the right values — only the editor display was wrong. This fix makes saved values visible and editable regardless of which event you open the editor from.

draft.docs_gap: The Field Rules guide should note that assignment rules referencing fields from other events display correctly in the editor, and explain the stale-option indicator ("<label> (not an option anymore)") that appears when a previously saved option has since been removed from a field.

entries.title: Disclosures: New form button hidden immediately for users without permission
entries.summary: Users who lack the Disclosures create permission no longer see the **New form** button at any point when opening **CRM → Disclosures → Forms**. Previously the button appeared for several seconds while the app retried a failed permission check, and clicking it produced a raw error toast. The no-access card now appears as soon as the list responds, with no error toast.

where.path: CRM → Disclosures → Forms

entries.use_case: Organizations that restrict Disclosures form creation to specific roles will no longer see restricted users briefly exposed to the **New form** button or receive confusing error toasts when the permission check resolves.

cs_action.note: Pure bug fix; no configuration change needed. The Disclosures feature flag and permission model are unchanged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that users without Disclosures access briefly saw the New form button or received a 403 error toast on the Forms tab.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Disclosures with role-based permission restrictions.
internal.staff_path: CRM → Disclosures → Forms
internal.gotchas: The fix relies on the org permission context being loaded before the tab renders; if the context is slow, the tab shows a loading state rather than the button — this is intentional.
internal.talk_track: The Disclosures Forms tab now respects role permissions immediately on load, so users without create access never see the New form button and won't encounter confusing error messages.

draft.docs_gap: The Disclosures guide should note which permission (Disclosures create) is required to see and use the New form button on the Forms tab.

entries.title: Saved view changes are recorded in History; Applications views save to the right view
entries.summary: Every saved view that is created, renamed, changed, deleted, or shared with the team or made private is now a row in the event or organization **History → Audit** log, under the **View** type (organization portal form submission views show as **Form submission view**). Columns, filters and sort are recorded as *changed*, never their contents. Also fixed: **Save Changes** and **Rename View** on an Applications saved view wrote to the default **Results** view instead of the view you were on.

where.path: History → Audit → Type: View or Form submission view

entries.use_case: When a shared view changes under a team — columns disappear, a filter is added — the audit log now says who did it and when, and a renamed or resaved Applications view no longer overwrites the team's default list.

cs_action.note: Nothing to enable. The Who can see this view (My team / Only me) controls that shipped in the same PRs are behind the super-user gate; customers see today's saved-views menu unchanged. A migration made every existing view a team view, so nobody lost a view.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks who changed or deleted a saved view, or reports that saving an Applications view replaced the Results view.
internal.who_should_get_it: Teams with several organizers sharing an event's saved views.
internal.staff_path: Event → History → Audit → Type filter → View. The My team / Only me switch: Saved views menu, super users only
internal.gotchas: The History filter label for organization portal form submission views is Form submission view (web-api #4779 fixed the row label to match). Only the creator of a view can change its visibility once the controls go GA; another person's private view is a 404, never a 403.
internal.talk_track: Every change to a saved view is now in the History log, so you can see who renamed or deleted the view your team relies on.

entries.title: Archive a past event without losing anything
entries.summary: A past event can now be archived. An archived event leaves the organization's **Events** page, the sidebar event switcher and event pickers, but nothing is deleted or switched off: its URL, portals, embeds, integrations and public API keep working. Inside the event a banner says it is archived and offers **Unarchive** to anyone with **Update Event Settings**. On the **Events** page, **Show archived** in the **Filter** popover (with a count) lists archived events with an **Archived** badge and an **Including archived** chip; the sidebar switcher has the same **Show archived** switch. Cloning an archived event produces a normal, unarchived event.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to archive the event; Event Settings → Details → Archive event

where.path: Event Settings → Details → Archive event; Events page → Filter → Show archived; sidebar event switcher → Show archived

entries.use_case: Teams that run many events year over year can keep the Events page and the switcher to what is live, while last year's event stays available for reporting, cloning and speaker history — and comes back with one click.

cs_action.note: The Archive event control in Event Settings → Details is staff-only during the rollout (lock badge). Customers cannot archive themselves yet; a staff user archives for them, and the banner, Unarchive and Show archived then appear to the customer on their own. Arizent asked for this (Community idea, 5 votes, 2 orgs).

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with a long Events list asks to hide past events without deleting them.
internal.who_should_get_it: High-volume, recurring-event customers (media companies, associations with many meetings).
internal.staff_path: Event → Event Settings → Details → Archive event (lock badge; needs Update Event Settings)
internal.gotchas: This is customer_archived_at, not the TAM lifecycle is_archived flag — the latter locks the event for every non-staff user and must not be used for this. Lite events have no Archive control in the UI yet. Reports, portfolio roll-ups and stats still include archived events; only lists hide them. The team access editor, bulk permissions and clone picker keep showing archived events on purpose.
internal.talk_track: We can archive last year's event for you: it drops out of your Events list and switcher, everything about it keeps working, and you can unarchive it yourself whenever you want.

entries.title: CFP submit form correctly identifies the account a submission is saved under
entries.summary: On the public session submission form, the **"You are logged in as"** banner and **"Welcome"** heading now show the portal account the submission will actually be attributed to — not the admin account open in the same browser. The inline disclosure check and the participant self-identification ("that's you") also use the correct identity.

where.path: Submit form → Account step → "You are logged in as" banner

entries.use_case: When an admin opens a CFP submission link while also signed into a speaker portal as a different person, the form now clearly shows which account will own the submission — preventing confusion about who the session is attributed to.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic; no configuration needed. The server's portal-first attribution logic is unchanged — only the UI label is corrected to match it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that a submission was saved under the wrong person, or that the 'You are logged in as' name on the submit form did not match the submitter recorded in the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose team members or speakers open CFP links while also logged in as an admin in the same browser.
internal.gotchas: The fix is web-UI only; no API change. The server has always attributed submissions to the portal bearer when one is present — this just makes the page say so. Admin session remains active; only the displayed identity on the submit form changes.
internal.talk_track: The submit form now tells submitters exactly which account their session will be filed under, so there is no surprise when the submission shows up under a portal user rather than the admin.

draft.docs_gap: The submission forms guide should note that when a portal magic-link session is active in the browser, the submit form attributes the submission to the portal user and displays that user's name in the "You are logged in as" banner.

entries.title: Session titles and speaker names in `{{{sessions_summary}}}` emails now render as plain text
entries.summary: The **`{{{sessions_summary}}}`** merge tag in **Send Email** and **Email Campaigns** now HTML-escapes the six default table columns — Session ID, Status, **Title**, Starts At, Ends At, and **Speakers** — so that special characters such as `&`, `<`, and `>` in session titles or speaker names are delivered as literal text rather than interpreted as markup by mail clients. Session titles like `Q&A` now appear correctly as `Q&A` in the rendered table.

where.path: Communications → Send Email or Email Campaigns → email body using {{{sessions_summary}}}

entries.use_case: Any event whose session titles or speaker names contain ampersands or angle brackets (e.g. medical comparisons like `>3 mg` or `Q&A` panels) will now have those characters displayed correctly in emailed session summary tables, without relying on mail-client error recovery.

cs_action.note: Two US titles (AACE event 5022, UKG Aspire event 5540) store a literal > — today those emails show > but after this fix they will show > as literal text, matching how the app UI already displays them. Flag to those accounts if they notice the change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that session titles or speaker names with special characters (ampersands, angle brackets) look wrong or render as HTML in their emailed session summary tables.
internal.who_should_get_it: All events using the {{{sessions_summary}}} merge tag — approximately 101 US events and 27 EU events identified in production. Particularly relevant for medical/scientific conferences with titles containing comparison operators or ampersands.
internal.gotchas: Two customer titles that stored a literal > entity will now display as > in email (instead of >) — this matches the app UI but is a visible change for those two events. Empty Status and Speakers cells still render as 'undefined'/'null' (known cosmetic issue, not addressed in this fix). ME region was not audited.
internal.talk_track: Session titles and speaker names submitted through CFP or portal forms are now always delivered as plain text in session summary emails — special characters like & or < in a title such as 'Q&A' or '<25 kg' display correctly in every mail client without depending on error recovery.

draft.docs_gap: The merge tags reference section should note that all default columns in the sessions_summary table are HTML-escaped, so special characters in titles and speaker names are always delivered as plain text.

entries.title: Closed submission forms now block new drafts and edits
entries.summary: When a submission form is closed with **Open for submissions = No**, the public submit page now shows the "Submissions closed" gate and the **Start submission** button is disabled. Attempting to save a new draft or edit an existing one returns an error: "Form submissions are no longer being accepted." The portal **Edit submission** link is also hidden for submissions on a closed form. Re-opening the form (**Open for submissions = Yes**) restores all access immediately.

where.path: Sessions → Forms → [form] → Open for submissions toggle; public submit link

entries.use_case: Organizers who close a form mid-cycle — for example to pause intake before a committee review — can now be confident that no new drafts slip through the public link after they flip the toggle off.

cs_action.note: Five live US production forms had is_enabled = false with no past close date and were silently accepting drafts before this fix. Check whether any of those customers have unexpected draft rows they need to know about.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer reports that speakers are still submitting after they closed the form, or asks how to pause intake without setting a close date.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers using session submission forms — fix is automatic, nothing to enable.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Forms → [form] → Settings → Open for submissions
internal.gotchas: Existing in-progress drafts on a closed form are also blocked from saving (same behaviour as a passed close date). Re-opening the form restores them. No data is deleted.
internal.talk_track: Flipping Open for submissions to No now locks the door completely — the public page shows a closed message, no new drafts can start, and anyone mid-draft cannot save until you re-open.

draft.docs_gap: The submission forms guide should note that setting Open for submissions = No immediately blocks the public submit page, new drafts, in-progress draft saves, and the portal Edit submission link — and that toggling back to Yes restores all access without touching existing data.

entries.title: "Evaluation" renamed to "Review" across the product
entries.summary: All human-facing labels that previously said "evaluation", "evaluator", or "judge" now read **Review**, **Reviewer**, or **My Reviews**. Affected surfaces include: **Program → Collect & Review** tabs (**Review plans**, **My reviews**, **Reviewers**, **Reviewer tags**, **Call for Reviewers**), the **Review summary** page, the **Reviewer portal**, Awards round settings and reviewer pages (no more "judge"), and the Agents **Reviewer** page whose AI persona is now labelled **Screener** with a **Re-screen** action. Attendee scoring strings use **Survey** wording. The navigation item formerly called "Preview" is now **Early Access**. Labels are updated in English, German, Spanish, and French.

where.path: Program → Collect & Review; Awards → Rounds; Agents → Reviewer

entries.use_case: Teams that use both the scoring and attendee-feedback features no longer have to explain the difference between "evaluations" and "surveys" — the product now uses distinct, self-explanatory terms: Review for committee scoring and Survey for attendee feedback.

cs_action.note: A companion API PR (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4785, SB-10526) ships the server-owned sidebar labels. Until both are deployed, the sidebar may briefly show old 'Evaluation' labels while page titles already read 'Review'. Coordinate deployment timing. Help Center manifest update is in lennd/sessionboard-docs#89 — docs pages still use old terminology until that ships.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any time a customer asks about the scoring or abstract-review workflow, or when onboarding a new program committee.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers using the scoring/review workflow; Awards customers who previously saw 'judge' in round settings.
internal.gotchas: de/es/fr translations were applied by rule and have not had a native-speaker review. Eight strings in the English bundle intentionally retain 'evaluat' (interpolation variables and Pathways example copy) — these are not regressions. The sidebar labels depend on the companion API PR deploying together.
internal.talk_track: We've standardised the language across the product: your committee members are Reviewers, the scoring process is a Review, and what attendees fill in after a session is a Survey. Nothing about how the feature works has changed — just the labels.

draft.docs_gap: All evaluation-related guide titles, headings, and body copy still use "evaluation" and "evaluator" — they need a find-and-replace pass to match the new "Review" / "Reviewer" nomenclature, including the article titles in the /evaluations/ folder and the Glossary entry.
draft.why_use_it: The Review module is where your program committee scores, ranks, and selects submissions before they become sessions. Reviewers work through their assigned submissions on a scorecard, and organizers track progress, manage conflicts of interest, and make final decisions — all in one place. Use it any time you need a structured, auditable scoring process separate from what attendees tell you after a session.

entries.title: Clearer names for Surveys, Participant Feedback, and the Screener context in Early Access
entries.summary: The **Early Access** catalogue now shows updated descriptions for two features. The **Surveys** card reads "Collect attendee feedback on sessions, speakers, and posters during the event…" (previously described scoring). The **Participant Feedback** card clarifies that it shows speakers their attendee survey results and is labelled **Early Access Beta**. In the AI context sidebar, the Team Lead label for the reviewer section now reads **Screener** instead of "Review Agent".

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Surveys / Participant Feedback

where.path: Settings → Early Access

entries.use_case: Organizers browsing Early Access now see accurate descriptions for Surveys and Participant Feedback, making it easier to understand what each feature does before opting in. The Screener label in the AI context sidebar matches the product's standard terminology.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is confused about the difference between Surveys (attendee feedback during the event) and evaluation plans, or asks what Participant Feedback shows speakers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer using or considering Surveys or Participant Feedback.
internal.staff_path: Admin Settings → Early Access
internal.gotchas: This is a copy-only change — no functional behaviour changed. The Screener label update is in the AI context sidebar only; the sidebar nav label itself is in a sibling PR (SB-10526).
internal.talk_track: The Early Access cards now say exactly what each feature does, so customers can make an informed decision about opting in without needing to ask support.

draft.docs_gap: The Early Access guide should note that the Surveys card describes during-event attendee feedback and that Participant Feedback surfaces those results to speakers, distinguishing both from evaluation plans.

entries.title: Edit live-session transcripts line by line: reassign speaker, split, insert and delete lines
entries.summary: Four new editing actions are available on live-session transcripts. **Change** on a single line's speaker popover now re-attributes only that line without affecting the speaker's other lines. A **Split here** action divides one line at the cursor into two. The **+** button inserts a new line above or below any existing line with its own speaker. A **Delete** (trash) action removes a mistaken split or inserted line. All changes persist on refresh and flow through to recaps, captions, exports and clips.

where.path: Marketing → Source & Produce → Transcribe → [live-session transcript]

entries.use_case: When a live-session transcript misidentifies a speaker on one line, or a single line contains words from two different people, editors can now fix it precisely — reassigning just that line, splitting it at the right word, or inserting a missed line — without disturbing the rest of the transcript.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that speaker attribution in a live-session transcript is wrong on individual lines, or that the Change button did nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Live Transcribe on session recordings, especially those who noticed the bug (e.g. NGA Executive Conference 2026).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Source & Produce → Transcribe → open a live-session transcript
internal.gotchas: These actions only work on transcripts captured in live-session mode. Transcripts bridged from a linked media recording (provider: 'media') return a 400 error — the customer must edit from the media profile instead. The companion UI PR (lennd/sessionboard-web-ui-v2, same branch) must also be deployed; API must go first.
internal.talk_track: You can now fix speaker attribution one line at a time — change who said a single sentence, split a line where two speakers overlap, add a line that was missed, or delete one that shouldn't be there. Everything downstream — recaps, captions, exports — picks up the correction automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the four per-line editing actions (Change speaker for one line, Split here, Insert line, Delete line) and note that they are unavailable on transcripts sourced from a linked media recording.

entries.title: Event Time Format now applies to portals, submission and follow-up forms, and admin grids
entries.summary: **Time Format** in [Event Details](/events/event-details#date--time) (12-hour or 24-hour) now sets the clock on the speaker, contact and account portals — task due dates, messages, file deadlines and uploads, session editing and profile time fields — on CFP deadlines, follow-up forms, and admin grids and session pages. The participant's language still sets month and day words but no longer decides 12-hour or 24-hour.

where.path: Speaker, contact and account portals (tasks, messages, session flyover, files, profile); CFP submission page; follow-up forms; admin grids and session pages

entries.use_case: Events that run on a 24-hour clock can set it once and see the same format on every portal page, CFP deadline and admin grid — no AM/PM on English-language portals, and no 24-hour times on a 12-hour event just because a speaker reads the portal in German or French.

cs_action.note: On 12-hour events (the default, ~97 % of live events), French- and German-language portal viewers will now see '2:05 PM' where they previously saw '14:05' from their browser locale. This is correct behaviour per the event setting, but organizers of European events who relied on the browser-locale fallback should set their event to 24-hour if they want 24-hour display.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any European or international event that has complained about AM/PM appearing in the portal or about inconsistent time display across surfaces.
internal.who_should_get_it: All events; especially European events that already have Time format set to 24-hour and were seeing inconsistent display.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Time format
internal.gotchas: The portal home Sessions and Calendar cards and follow-up form times are formatted by web-api (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4804) and follow the setting only once that ships in a web-api release. Exports use the separate Export date format setting. A browser's own pop-up time picker follows the device and can't be forced. Some admin views (agenda list and calendar cards, the activity tab, Review screens, sequence dialogs) still show 12-hour times until the web-ui-v2 follow-up (fix/admin-time-format) merges.
internal.talk_track: Set your event's time format once in Event Settings and every surface your speakers and reviewers touch — portal tasks, session editors, CFP deadlines, admin grids — will show times consistently in 12- or 24-hour format.

entries.title: Org CRM field permissions now enforced on inline edits and profile saves
entries.summary: Org role permissions for **Contacts** and **Accounts** — including **Edit** access, locked fields, and hidden fields — are now enforced when a team member edits a contact cell inline in the org contacts grid, saves a contact profile, saves an account profile, or updates contact address/header fields. Previously, any org member could write these values regardless of their role. Now, a member without **Contacts Edit** or **Contacts Manage** receives a 403 and the cell reverts; a locked field returns a 403; a hidden field returns a 404. Event-level edits are unchanged.

where.path: Org → Contacts (grid inline edit and contact profile); Org → Accounts (account profile)

entries.use_case: Orgs that restrict certain team members to read-only access on contacts or accounts can now trust that restriction holds on every edit surface — inline grid cells, contact profiles, account profiles, and address fields — not only the bulk edit sidebar.

cs_action.note: The fix is a security correction — no one who was actively editing in the last 90 days loses access (verified against prod audit logs). However, members whose org role has neither Contacts Update nor Contacts Manage will now receive a 403 on inline edits and profile saves. The UI reverts the cell automatically. A follow-up UI change to hide the inline edit control for read-only roles is planned but not yet shipped.
