internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why a team member's inline contact or account edit is now being rejected, or when discussing org role permissions and field-level locks.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any CRM customer who uses custom org roles with restricted Contacts or Accounts permissions, or who uses locked/hidden field settings under Settings → Permissions.
internal.staff_path: Org → Settings → Permissions → [org role] → Fields (to configure locked/hidden fields)
internal.gotchas: Program Manager is the default org role and has Contacts Manage but not Contacts Update — these users retain edit access. Members with a role that has neither Update nor Manage on Contacts (or Accounts) will now get a 403 on saves. Prod data shows zero such members made org-level edits in the last 90 days, so real-world impact is expected to be minimal. The inline grid cell reverts on 403 automatically; no UI change is needed on the customer side.
internal.talk_track: Org role permissions and field locks now apply consistently everywhere in the org CRM — inline grid edits, profile saves, and address fields — matching the behaviour already in place for bulk edits.

draft.docs_gap: The org roles and field permissions guide should note that hidden and locked field settings, and the Contacts/Accounts Edit permission, now apply to inline grid edits and profile saves in the org CRM, not only the bulk edit sidebar.

entries.title: Preview as… now lists attendee and group recipients in Advocacy campaigns
entries.summary: The **Preview as…** button on an Advocacy campaign page now lists all recipient types — contacts (speakers), attendees, and group (exhibitor/sponsor) recipients — matching what the per-row **View as** action already showed. Previously, the dialog incorrectly showed "No recipients assigned yet" for campaigns whose recipients were imported as attendees or added as groups, even though those recipients appeared on the **Recipients** tab.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign] → Preview as…

entries.use_case: Organizers running attendee or exhibitor/sponsor Advocacy campaigns can now use **Preview as…** to verify exactly what each recipient sees before the campaign goes live, without having to click through individual rows on the Recipients tab.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that Preview as… shows no recipients on an attendee or exhibitor/sponsor Advocacy campaign.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy with attendee CSV imports or group (exhibitor/sponsor) recipients.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Advocacy → [campaign] → Preview as…
internal.gotchas: The fix is client-side only; no API change. The footer text 'N total assigned (including groups)' has been removed since groups now appear directly in the list.
internal.talk_track: If you have been using the per-row View as workaround to preview attendee or group recipient links, the header Preview as… button now works the same way for all recipient types.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that Preview as… supports all recipient kinds — contacts, attendees, and groups — and explain how to use it to verify the share experience before launch.

entries.title: Portals with mismatched forms can be edited again
entries.summary: A contact portal that already held a Group (accounts-module) form assigned before module validation was introduced would return a **400 "Failed to assign items."** error on every save — including reorders and new additions — leaving the portal stuck. The fix grandfathers already-assigned forms: organizers can now add, reorder, and remove forms on those portals without error. Adding a new mismatched form still returns a 400 and now names the offending form.

where.path: Portals → [portal] → Customize → Assign Items → Forms

entries.use_case: Any organizer whose contact portal was silently assigned a Group form in the past and could no longer add or reorder forms can now manage that portal normally without needing to delete and recreate it.

cs_action.note: 55 portals / 107 form rows on US prod are in this state (EU: 0). Identify affected customers and let them know the portal is editable again. The companion web-ui-v2 PR will add a 'Not for this portal' badge on the legacy mismatched forms once deployed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports 'Failed to assign items.' on a contact portal or says they cannot reorder or add forms to an existing portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer on US prod with a contact portal that held a Group form before module validation was added — 55 portals identified on US prod.
internal.staff_path: Portals → [affected portal] → Customize → Assign Items → Forms
internal.gotchas: The fix only grandfathers forms already in the database for that portal. Adding a brand-new Group form to a contact portal still returns a 400 (by design). The UI's form picker does not offer Group forms on People portals, so this is API-only for new additions.
internal.talk_track: A past data state was causing every save on certain contact portals to fail. The portal is now fully editable again — you can add, reorder, and remove forms as normal.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that forms must match the portal's module type, and that legacy mismatched forms already assigned to a portal are grandfathered and will display a badge indicating they are not intended for that portal type.

entries.title: Forms panel flags mismatched legacy forms and shows the API's error message
entries.summary: On a People portal's **Assign Items → Forms** panel, any form whose module does not match the portal (for example, a Group form assigned before module validation existed) now shows a **Not for this portal** badge with a tooltip explaining the mismatch and prompting removal. When adding or reordering forms fails, the error toast now shows the exact message returned by the API (for example, "forms must match this portal's module … : New Form 7") instead of the generic "Failed to assign items."

where.path: Portals → [portal] → Customize → Assign Items → Forms

entries.use_case: Organizers who inherited a People portal with a legacy Group form assigned can now immediately see which forms are mismatched and remove them, unblocking the ability to add or reorder other forms without cryptic error messages.

cs_action.note: Visible to all organizers automatically once web-api #4803 is deployed; the badge only renders when the API returns module_id on assigned forms.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports being unable to add or reorder forms on a contact portal, or sees 'Failed to assign items' with no explanation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer with a People portal that was configured before module validation was introduced — most likely older accounts.
internal.staff_path: Portals → [People portal] → Customize → Assign Items → Forms
internal.gotchas: The 'Not for this portal' badge only appears after web-api #4803 is live and serving module_id on form objects. Until then, the panel looks unchanged but the improved error toast is already active.
internal.talk_track: If you've ever been stuck unable to add forms to a contact portal with a confusing error, the panel now tells you exactly which form is the problem and why, so you can remove it and move on.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that forms must match the portal's module type and explain what the "Not for this portal" badge means and how to resolve it.
draft.why_use_it: Portal forms let you collect structured information from speakers, sponsors, or other participants directly inside their portal experience. Assigning the right forms to the right portal type keeps the participant experience clean and ensures submissions land in the correct module. The forms panel gives admins full control over which forms appear, in what order, and for whom.

entries.title: Bulk edit now saves a checkbox field as "No" without requiring a workaround
entries.summary: In the **Bulk Edit** sidebar, selecting a checkbox field and leaving the switch at **No** now enables the **Save** button immediately. Clicking **Save** opens the **Confirm Bulk Edit** dialog and sets the field to **No** on all selected records. Previously, the **Save** button stayed disabled until the switch was flipped to **Yes** and back to **No**.

where.path: CRM → All Contacts → select records → Edit; Sessions → select records → Edit

entries.use_case: Organizers who need to bulk-set a checkbox field to "No" across many contacts or sessions can now do so in a single action without first toggling the switch on and off as a workaround.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that bulk-setting a checkbox to No does nothing or requires a toggle workaround.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer using Bulk Edit on contacts or sessions with checkbox fields.
internal.staff_path: Event → CRM or Sessions → select records → Edit → pick a checkbox field
internal.gotchas: The fix only changes the dialog's initial state and Save gating; the API payload is unchanged. Sessions grid Bulk Edit (same component) is also fixed.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that selecting a checkbox field in Bulk Edit treats the switch position itself as the value, so leaving it at "No" is a valid, saveable choice.

entries.title: Clearer message when a session submission form has been deleted
entries.summary: When a session submission form has been deleted, the public submission page now shows **"This submission form is no longer available."** instead of the generic view-only copy. Visitors who already submitted see their answers read-only with a banner: **"This submission form is no longer available. If you submitted through it, your submission is shown below, read-only. Contact the event organizer if you need to make changes."**

where.path: Public submission form link (Call for Papers page)

entries.use_case: When an organizer deletes a submission form, anyone who opens the public link now immediately understands the form is gone — rather than seeing a confusing "view-only" message that implies editing was simply disabled.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that speakers are confused by the read-only state on a deleted submission form.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers who use session submission forms; no action needed.
internal.gotchas: The new message only appears when the API returns is_form_deleted: true (requires web-api #4801). Sponsor/exhibitor view-only forms on live (non-deleted) forms still show the original read-only copy — this change is scoped to deleted CFP forms only.
internal.talk_track: Speakers who click a link to a deleted submission form now see a clear explanation instead of a generic read-only notice.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note what submitters see when a form is deleted and how to restore a form from Trash to re-enable submissions.
